summary: The note describes the Finnish Navy's actions at the start of the Winter War against the Soviet Union. It covers the occupation of the demilitarized Åland Islands, battles between Soviet ships and Finnish coastal batteries in the first month, failed submarine attacks, and the freezing of the sea in December 1939. It ends with the coastal defence ships being moved to Turku to support air defence.
one_line: Overview of the Finnish Navy's early Winter War operations, including coastal battles, failed submarine attacks, and winter ice conditions.
key_facts: When the Winter War broke out, the Finnish Navy moved to occupy the de-militarized Åland Islands and to protect merchant shipping.
In the first month of the Winter War, battles between Soviet ships and Finnish coastal batteries were fought at Hanko, Finland, Utö and Koivisto.
At Koivisto and Hanko, Finnish coastal batteries forced Soviet battleships to retire with damage.
Finnish efforts to use submarines named "Vesikko" and "Saukko" to sink Soviet capital ships failed.
In December 1939 the ice became so thick that only the ice-breakers could still move.
The two coastal defence ships were moved to the harbour in Turku.
In Turku, the two coastal defence ships were used to strengthen the air-defences of the city.
The two coastal defence ships remained in Turku for the rest of the war.
